newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASEAN had to do more than delay Cambodia-minister.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN had to do more than delay Cambodia-minister.

text.p: The Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) has to do more than just delay war-torn Cambodia's entry into the group -- it wants to ensure peace there first, Singapore's foreign minister was quoted as saying.

ASEAN on Thursday postponed Cambodia's entry, originally scheduled for this month, saying it still recognised Prince Norodom Ranariddh as co-premier, despite his ouster by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen on Sunday.

"(ASEAN) foreign ministers felt today that ASEAN would not be doing enough if all they did was to settle the question of timing," Friday's Straits Times quoted Foreign Minister Shanmugam Jayakumar as saying.
"For ASEAN to be a serious organisation, we must go further."
Before Cambodia was admitted, there had to be an end to bloodshed, a functioning coalition government and scheduled elections, the paper quoted Jayakumar as saying.
General elections are due next May.

Jayakumar was speaking to Singapore reporters in Kuala Lumpur, where ASEAN foreign ministers met on Thursday, agreeing to send a delegation to meet Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk and the feuding prime ministers in an effort to end the crisis.

ASEAN's statement on Thursday reiterated the group's policy of not interfering in a neighbouring country's internal affairs, but said the use of force in ousting Ranariddh made it necessary to delay Cambodia's entry.
At least 58 people were killed and up to 200 wounded last weekend in clashes between forces loyal to Hun Sen and those with Ranariddh.
ASEAN groups Singapore, Malaysia, the Philippines, Vietnam, Brunei, Thailand and Indonesia.
